Subject: Tokyo pilot - dedicated capacity needs and traffic profile

Hi Soojin,

Thanks again for the demo last week — team loved the latency and routing controls. We're ready to scope a small dedicated pilot in Tokyo to validate local latency and data residency. High-level asks below:

- Goal: <10ms median latency to Tokyo app servers, p95 <80ms for inference.
- Traffic: initial pilot targets ~7k sessions/day, ~120 requests/minute peak. Attached a sample traffic_profile.csv (per-request tokens included).
- Model: planning to run a 13B family open model (approx 32GB FP16).
- Duration: 60-day pilot, with potential to convert to a committed pool (reserved nodes) at the end.
- Compliance: Japan data residency required for logs and KV cache.

Questions for Redwood:
1) Recommended node/sku for this workload (H100 vs A100 options) for predictable p95 and burst handling?
2) Rough monthly committed hours / node count we should budget for conversion to Dedicated.
3) Typical lead times for enabling a new APAC region/pilot and any compliance checklist items.

I've attached the traffic_profile.csv and a short SOW draft for context. Would prefer a single short call next week to align on sizing.

Best,
Yuki

From: soojin_lee@redwood.com

Subject: Re: Tokyo pilot - dedicated capacity needs and traffic profile

Hi Yuki — thanks for the detail and the CSV, that's helpful. Quick summary/proposal after an initial pass:

TL;DR: For a 60-day Tokyo pilot running a 13B FP16 model with your peak profile, we recommend a 2-node dedicated pilot (H100-equivalent) with automatic burst to 4 nodes for traffic spikes. If you convert to a long-term reserved pool we estimate a steady-state commitment of 2 nodes (24/7) with a burst buffer of +2 nodes.

Sizing rationale / assumptions:
- Traffic: ~120 req/minute peak, average request ~800 tokens (from CSV) -> steady-state ~1.6k tok/s, bursts up to ~3.2k tok/s.
- Throughput: a single H100-equivalent node (our optimized runtime) can sustain ~1.2–1.8k tok/s at p95 targets for that model family depending on quantization and prompt shape.
- Buffering: we recommend 2 nodes to hit p95 goals and allow headroom; burst policy to add 2 nodes when 80% saturation observed.

Options (cost vs latency):
A) H100-dedicated (recommended): 2 nodes steady, burst to 4. Best p95 and headroom; faster time-to-convert to Reserved.
B) A100-40GB (fallback): 3 nodes steady (higher steady count) to match p95; cheaper to source short-term but larger pool count.

Next steps I propose:
1) Short 30-min sizing call Tue/Wed next week to confirm traffic windows and acceptable p95 targets (I'll send invite).
2) We'll prepare a pilot SOW + proposed committed-hours quote (ballpark before legal).
3) Karthik — can you confirm lead times for spinning up a new Tokyo pilot in a customer VPC and any hardware procurement constraints?
4) Irene — note Kokoro requires logs/KV residency in Japan; flag any missing compliance bits.

I'll attach a compact sizing spreadsheet and a draft SOW after the call.

Best,
Soojin Lee
Account Executive — APAC
Redwood Inference
--

Hi Yuki — quick update and agreed next steps after internal checks. Thanks for the patience.

What we're proposing for the 60-day Tokyo pilot (summary):
- Pilot footprint: 2 x H100-equivalent nodes steady with automatic burst to +2 nodes (4 total) when queue depth crosses 80%.
- If H100 inventory is tight at time of provisioning, fallback is 3 x A100-40GB steady, burst +1 (total 4). We'll note both options in the SOW.
- Expected steady throughput: ~1.6k tok/s (meets median <10ms and p95 targets with 2 H100 nodes for your observed token shapes).
- Data residency: logs and KV cache will be kept in our Tokyo region for the pilot; control plane will remain in our standard APAC control plane with restricted access. Irene will attach a checklist for the SOW.

Deliverables and timeline:
- SOW v1 (attached): includes commitment window, pilot acceptance criteria, and conversion options to Reserved Pool.
- Provisioning ETA: typically 10–14 business days for VPC-onboard in Tokyo if H100 is available. If A100 fallback used we can often provision in 5–7 business days.
- Pricing: we'll send a ballpark committed-hours quote post-call (Karthik to confirm final node-hour rates).

Immediate asks for Kokoro:
- Please confirm you accept the pilot footprint (2xH100 steady, burst to 4) or if you'd prefer we price the A100 fallback instead.
- Sign SOW v1 (I've included a DocuSign link below) or propose edits.
- Confirm a 30-min kickoff window next Tue (2027-08-24) 02:00–05:00 UTC (we'll align to JST on the invite).
